question:
When the pytest test
`kedro_qa/omegaconf_config_load_and_merge_dir_config_s2_loops/files/testcase.py::TestOmegaConfDirMergeLoops::test_traced_run`
is executed, the function
`kedro.config.omegaconf_config.OmegaConfigLoader.load_and_merge_dir_config`
(defined in the repository file `kedro/config/omegaconf_config.py`) is
invoked several times. Constructing the `OmegaConfigLoader` in the test

loads the `globals` configuration from the conf source root directory).
The test body then calls `load_and_merge_dir_config` directly three more
times, once per generated configuration directory, in the order
`phase_a`, `phase_b`, `phase_c`.

Invocation counting: invocations of
`kedro.config.omegaconf_config.OmegaConfigLoader.load_and_merge_dir_config`
are counted 1-based, in chronological order of function entry, where one
invocation is one entry into the function (one `call` event as seen by a
line-level execution tracer) during the test run. The three direct calls
in the test body are therefore invocations 2, 3 and 4.

Focus on the inner `for` loop whose header is at line 334 of
`kedro/config/omegaconf_config.py` (the loop
`for each in self._fs.glob(...):`, nested inside the outer loop
`for pattern in patterns:` at line 333; line numbers are absolute and
1-based in the file as it exists on disk in this repository). Define one
iteration of this loop as one execution of the first line of the loop
body (i.e. the first physical line nested under the loop header). Every
match produced by `self._fs.glob(...)` drives one iteration, including
matches that are later discarded: hidden paths, directories, files whose
extension is not YAML or JSON, and paths that were already produced by an
earlier pattern (de-duplication happens only after both loops finish).
If the loop body never executes, the iteration count is 0.

Task: report the exact number of iterations of the loop at line 334
during the 3rd invocation of
`kedro.config.omegaconf_config.OmegaConfigLoader.load_and_merge_dir_config`
in this test run (that is, the direct call on the `phase_b` directory).

Answer format: a JSON object with exactly one key, `loop_iteration_count`,
whose value is a single integer (a JSON number, not a string).
